# data/larian — game data (generated)

**Generated — do not edit by hand.** Every file in this folder except this README is written by the import command from the installed game's files, read-only.

> Non-commercial fan project; content owned by Larian Studios.

## Provenance

- Game: Baldur's Gate 3, version 4.1.1.7631656 (patch 8); the exact version is also in `meta.json`.
- Rules: the LSX and stats files of the `Shared.pak`, `Gustav.pak` and `GustavX.pak` paks, modules `Shared`, `SharedDev`, `Gustav`, `GustavDev`, `GustavX` in that override order. Mod paks and Honour mode modules are ignored; a hotfix pak (`Data/Patch*.pak`) that touches rules files stops the import.
- Items: the scope is the obtainable items (`legacy` null) of `data/wiki/items.json` (bg3.wiki, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0), minus `scripts/data/items_excluded.txt`; each is looked up in the item stats (`Armor.txt`, `Weapon.txt`) by its identifier, its stats entry's `RootTemplate` giving its template; failing that, as the `Name` of the RootTemplate (`RootTemplates/_merged.lsf` of the same modules) given by its wiki `uuid`, that template's `Stats` giving its stats entry. Its name and description come from that template. The items the equipment lists (`SelectEquipment`) offer outside that scope are added from their stats entry and its `RootTemplate` (`found_by: "list"`): the six weapons of the weapon list and the five instruments of the instrument list. Every item carries its stats entry's `Weapon Properties` (`properties`); a weapon without any is an import error. `scripts/data/lsf.py` reads the binary LSF templates (ported from LSLib, MIT) and `scripts/data/templates.py` applies overrides and `ParentTemplateId` inheritance across the modules. Real counts at import: 1368 wiki items, 744 with locations, 1178 items imported (519 found by stats, 648 by template, 11 from the equipment lists).
- Origins: `Origins/Origins.lsx` of the same modules (a later module replaces an origin of the same UUID), minus `scripts/data/origins_excluded.txt`; class, subclass, race and subrace resolved to their rules keys, the background kept as its UUID; base scores from `CharacterCreationPresets/AbilityDistributionPresets.lsx`, the preset of the subclass if there is one, else of the class. A reference that does not resolve, or a subclass that is not a subclass of the origin's class, is an error unless `scripts/data/origin_references.txt` replaces or drops it.
- Rulesets: `Ruleset/Rulesets.lsx`, `Ruleset/RulesetModifiers.lsx` and `Ruleset/RulesetValues.lsx` of the same modules; only the rulesets with `ShowInCustom="true"` (Explorer, Balanced, Tactician, Standard and Honour rulesets), each with its `order` (position in the game's file; the JSON keys are sorted) and its values for the three build modifiers `MULTICLASSING`, `PROFICIENCY_BONUS` and `HONOUR_STATS` (a modifier without a value keeps its default, given by `rulesetModifiers` with its type, bounds and whether the custom-mode screen shows it). Every other modifier is ignored; an unexpected modifier type, a value of the wrong type or outside its bounds, or a value naming an unknown ruleset or modifier is an error. The label `label:customMode` ("Custom Mode") comes from a fixed translation handle.
- Texts: the English and French translation tables (`Localization/English.pak`, `Localization/French/French.pak`). Texts are kept raw (markup and parameters included). Skill and ability names have no handle in any data file read: they come from two indexed families of translation entries in the engine's enum order (`h65e11968gf9b6g4c47g9efcg03fb60fb923c_0`…`_17` for the 18 skills, `h6c83537fg6358g41e0g8a18g32cc8316ced2_1`…`_6` for the six abilities; see `scripts/data/ui_names.py`). Each entry's English text must equal the label derived from its identifier (`SleightOfHand` → `Sleight of Hand`, compared case-insensitively), so a change of order fails the import. Skill descriptions, equipment slot names and damage type names come from the PC interface files of `Game.pak` (`Public/Game/GUI/Library/Tooltips.xaml` and `Public/Game/GUI/Library/CharacterSheetTemplates.xaml`, read for these texts only; see `scripts/data/gui.py`): each is the translation handle of the first setter of a `DataTrigger` on `{Binding Skill}` (setter on `Description`), `{Binding SelectedSlotType}` (setter on `Text`) or `{Binding DamageType}` (setter on the `DamageType` element's `Text`; the colour triggers are ignored). Every skill, each of the 16 planned slots and each of the 13 damage types must have exactly one handle present in both tables, and a hotfix pak holding one of the two files stops the import.

## Files

- `meta.json`: game version, modules read, and the ownership notice in English and French (shown by the app in each language).
- `rules.json`: classes and subclasses, playable races, backgrounds, feats, progressions, the lists they reference, spells and passives (with their boosts, and `technical: true` on the passives listed in `scripts/data/technical_passives.txt`), the origins (`class`, `subclass`, `race`, `subrace`, `background`, `lockRace`, `abilities`), the rulesets (`values`) and the build modifiers (`rulesetModifiers`), and the key items (`kind`, `found_by` — `stats`, `template` or `list`, the lookup that found the item —, `stats_type`, `slot`, `rarity`, `root_template`, `properties` — the weapon properties in file order, empty for armour). `spells.*.level` is `null` when the game's stats give the spell no `Level`; an item's `slot` or `rarity` is `null` when its stats entry has none.
- `texts.en.json`, `texts.fr.json`: name and description of every element, keyed `<category>:<identifier>`; also `origin:<Name>`, `skill:<Id>` for the items of the skill lists (name and the interface's description) and `ability:<Ability>` for the six abilities (names only, null description), `slot:<Id>` for the 16 equipment slots the planner uses (`Helmet`, `Cloak`, `Breast`, `Gloves`, `Boots`, `Amulet`, `Ring`, `Ring2`, `MeleeMainHand`, `MeleeOffHand`, `RangedMainHand`, `RangedOffHand`, `MusicalInstrument`, `VanityBody`, `VanityBoots`, `Underwear`; names only, as the tables write them, not upper-cased), `damage:<Type>` for the 13 damage types (names only), `ruleset:<Name>` (name and description), `modifier:<Name>` (name and description) for the build modifiers the game names (`MULTICLASSING`, `PROFICIENCY_BONUS`) and `label:customMode` (name only).

## Command

```
python3.14 -m scripts.data.importer --game <game install directory> --game-version <version> --output data/larian
```

`--game` defaults to `$BG3_GAME`; `--wiki` (the bg3.wiki item file) defaults to `data/wiki/items.json`. The import fails, writing nothing, on any duplicate identifier, orphan reference or missing text, and prints the complete list.

Eight committed lists, each entry with its reason, describe the exceptions found in the source data (the game's files, or the bg3.wiki items for `items_excluded.txt` and `ambiguous_uids.txt`); an entry that no longer matches the data is an error, so each list stays exact:

- `scripts/data/unnamed.txt`: identifiers deliberately left without a name; a line `<identifier> description` instead keeps the name (required in both languages) and leaves the description knowingly missing (`null` in both text tables).
- `scripts/data/game_typos.txt`: typos in the game's own progression or feat selectors, each corrected before parsing, only on an exact match of the raw segment. Nothing else is ever corrected.
- `scripts/data/items_excluded.txt`: 57 obtainable bg3.wiki items kept out of the imported items because neither lookup finds them in the game data, or because the wiki and the game disagree on them; an entry that is not an obtainable wiki item, or that now resolves without error, is an error. Four groups: 39 whose wiki uuid is not a RootTemplate (36 of them named `S_*`, likely placed level objects); 11 whose wiki uuid's RootTemplate has another `Name`; 1 whose template `Stats` is neither armour nor weapon; 6 found by stats name whose wiki uuid differs from the stats entry's RootTemplate.
- `scripts/wiki/ambiguous_uids.txt`: the 6 wiki uids shared by several different items, left out of `data/wiki/items.json` together with their locations because a location cannot be attributed by uid; a listed uid that is no longer ambiguous is an error.
- `scripts/data/origins_excluded.txt`: origins (`Name`) left out of `rules.json` (test, debug or other non-playable entries).
- `scripts/data/origin_references.txt`: `<origin> <class|subclass|race|subrace> <rules key>` for an origin reference the game gives wrongly, either a non-playable element (Astarion's `UndeadHighElfHidden` subrace → `Elf_HighElf`) or a subclass that is not a subclass of the origin's class; `-` as the key drops the reference (`Hireling_Wizard subclass -`: the game gives a Sorcerer subclass to a Wizard; the abilities then come from the class preset). A listed key must fit the origin (a base class, a subclass of its class, a base race, a subrace of its race); an entry whose reference has no such problem, whose key is missing or does not fit, or whose origin is unknown or excluded is an error. There is no automatic fallback to a parent race.
- `scripts/data/technical_passives.txt`: passives the interface hides (engine toggles, unlocks, messages); each is marked `technical: true`, and a listed name that is not a passive of the rules is an error. `python3.14 -m scripts.data.checks data/larian --technical-candidates` prints, grouped, the passives not yet listed whose name is missing, empty or starts with a lowercase letter in either language, for the maintainer to review.
- `scripts/data/known_duplicates.txt`: groups of progressions that share the same table, level and multiclass flag in the game itself. They are kept unchanged in `rules.json`; the rules engine applies every row of a group and counts a selector identical to one of an earlier row once (the rule and its bg3.wiki sources are stated in that file).

`python3.14 -m scripts.data.checks data/larian` checks the committed data without the game (references, texts, counts, selectors, duplicates, items against the wiki scope and the equipment lists, weapon properties, origins, technical passives, and the keys of `data/rules/skills.json` against the skill lists).
